title: Selfish and prosocial individuals both distort their actions’ impact, but selfish distortions can be more contagious
title_zh: 利己与利他个体均会扭曲其行为影响，但利己扭曲更易传播
abstract: Abstract People often act without knowing exactly how their actions impact others. Here, across nine preregistered online experiments ( N = 8,769 adults, predominantly US residents), we tested whether people exploit this ambiguity to make themselves look good. On average, selfish individuals inflated the social benefit of their choice while downplaying that of the alternative, reporting the two options as more similar than prosocial individuals did (experiment 1a: b = 0.24, 95% confidence interval 0.14–0.34). Prosocial individuals portrayed their choice as comparatively more socially beneficial; they also inflated their implied relative sacrifice, although less consistently. We observed distortions even before people made a choice and when choices were forced, consistent with distortions reflecting social preferences rather than mere justification. While people differed in whether and how they distorted, distortions favouring selfishness showed evidence of contagion: others adopted them and became more selfish (experiment 6, selfish-serving versus no-distortion: b = 0.49, 95% confidence interval 0.10–0.88). These findings offer a psychological foundation for why polarized positions about the social impact of one’s actions may emerge. When social consequences are open to interpretation, people may predictably form divergent interpretations.
abstract_zh: 摘要 人们常常在不完全了解自己行为对他人影响的情况下行动。本研究在九项预注册在线实验中（N = 8,769名成人，主要为美国居民）检验了人们是否利用这种模糊性来让自己看起来更好。平均而言，利己个体夸大了自己选择的社会效益，同时淡化了替代方案的效益，报告两种选项的差异比利他个体更小（实验1a：b = 0.24，95%置信区间 0.14–0.34）。利他个体则将自己的选择描绘为更具社会效益；他们也夸大了相对牺牲，尽管不够一致。我们观察到即使在人们做出选择之前以及在强制选择时也存在扭曲，这与扭曲反映的是社会偏好而非单纯的辩解相符。虽然人们在是否以及如何扭曲上存在差异，但利己倾向的扭曲表现出传播效应：他人采纳了这些扭曲并变得更利己（实验6，利己服务型与无扭曲：b = 0.49，95%置信区间 0.10–0.88）。这些发现为为何关于自身行为社会影响的极化立场会出现提供了心理学基础。当社会后果开放解释时，人们可能会可预测地形成不同的解释。
